claims.wording: Historians of the silver trade generally explain the Manila trade by China's demand for silver. Silver was worth more in Ming China than anywhere else. Spanish America produced it at low cost. From 1571 Manila gave the two a direct meeting place. Flynn and Giráldez (1995), Atwell (1982) and von Glahn (1996) all explain it this way.
claims.notes:
Quote: "it was the elevated value of silver inside China that created the opportunities for profit around the globe" (Flynn and Giráldez 1995, p. 206); "Manila was the crucial entrepôt linking substantial, direct, and continuous trade between America and Asia for the first time in history." (Flynn and Giráldez 1995, p. 201); "render Spanish American mines the world's lowest cost sources of silver" (Flynn and Giráldez 1995, p. 209); "Silver poured into China because the Chinese market valued it more highly than anywhere else in the world" (von Glahn, *Fountain of Fortune*, ch. 4, p. 133); "foreign traders found the Chinese demand for silver almost insatiable" (Atwell 1982, p. 79)
